output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: none

Mick, please don't go into 43 at 9. It's a kind offer, but it's the worst place to be standing right now.

I'm a chartered structural engineer, but this isn't a commission and I'm only speaking as a neighbour who looked from the pavement at 7. The roof of 43 is holed over the front bedroom. There's a stepped crack running up from the bay, and about 1.2m of the stack from 41 is still standing, leaning towards 43 with the mortar washed out at the base. Gusts of 50mph are forecast again this afternoon. Anyone underneath that is at risk.

With debris sitting on the floors, nobody knows how the load is getting down any more. Props in the wrong place can make things worse. Please don't go up into the loft from inside either. Leave it to the council's dangerous structures team.

---

To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p04
Cc: none
Subject: none

Priya, same caveat as above: I'm a neighbour who looked from the pavement at 7, and this isn't formal advice.

The pavement isn't OK. The council tape only covers your front garden, not the footway. There are loose slates along the gutter line of 43 and 45 directly over the pavement, and the rest of the stack could come down in the wind. Please walk on the other side of the road until the council has been, especially on the school run. The council knows about the chimney, but nobody has closed the footway. Out of hours, the route is the council's main number, so it's worth ringing and saying that.

Mrs Doherty: it's not my decision and I can't see inside. But I wouldn't sleep in the front room tonight, and I'd rather she went to family until 45 has been checked. The front of 45 looks undamaged from the street, but I couldn't see the party wall with 43.

JoJo, your cousin is right that Victorian terraces are generally robust. This one has been damaged, though, and that's a different thing.
